Calculate purity thresholds

Source: R/get_purity.R
get_agilent_threshold.Rd

Computes the threshold used by get_purity: the similarity expected between a spectrum and the reference if they differed only by noise, the product of their reliabilities \((1 - \sigma^2_{noise} / \sigma^2_i)(1 - \sigma^2_{noise} / \sigma^2_{ref})\), capped at max_threshold.

Usage

get_agilent_threshold(
  x,
  pos,
  noise_inflation = 1,
  noise_variance = NULL,
  noise_method = c("quantile", "threshold"),
  noise_quantile = 0.1,
  noise_window = NULL,
  noise_threshold = NULL,
  max_threshold = 0.99,
  background_correction = c("linear", "constant", "none"),
  reference = c("average", "apex"),
  cutoff = 0.05,
  lambdas,
  weight = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A chromatographic matrix (timepoints × wavelengths).

pos

A length-3 integer vector c(apex, start, end) giving the row indices of the peak apex, left boundary, and right boundary in x.

noise_inflation

Multiplier applied to the noise variance. Defaults to 1.

noise_variance

Variance of noise.

noise_method

How to select the timepoints used to estimate the noise variance. Either "quantile" or "threshold".

noise_quantile

Quantile of maximum absorbance below which timepoints are treated as noise.

noise_window

Optional range of row indices to use as the noise region.

noise_threshold

Threshold to define noise. Used only when noise_method == "threshold", where NULL (the default) means 0.005.

max_threshold

Ceiling on the threshold. Defaults to 0.99.

background_correction

How to correct the peak spectra for background absorbance. Either "linear", "constant", or "none".

reference

Which spectrum to compare against. Either "average" (the default) or "apex". See get_purity.

cutoff

Proportion of the corrected apex height below which timepoints are excluded from the average reference spectrum. Defaults to 0.05.

lambdas

Wavelengths to include. Character values are matched to the column names of x; numeric values are taken as column indices.

weight

The weight argument is deprecated. Please use noise_inflation instead.

Value

Returns a vector of purity thresholds, one for each timepoint from the start to the end of the peak specified by pos, or NULL if the peak cannot be assessed.

References

Stahl, Mark. “Peak Purity Analysis in HPLC and CE Using Diode-Array Technology.” Agilent Technologies, April 1, 2003, 16. 5988-8647EN.pdf

Author

Ethan Bass

Examples

data(Sa_warp)
x <- Sa_warp[[1]]
pos <- c(37, 22, 51)
get_agilent_threshold(x, pos)
#>  [1] 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.6221288 0.8321277 0.9184135
#>  [8] 0.9579810 0.9755804 0.9831036 0.9863842 0.9878527 0.9885007 0.9887190
#> [15] 0.9886271 0.9881708 0.9870904 0.9847495 0.9795133 0.9667497 0.9359573
#> [22] 0.8829043 0.8173311 0.7015591 0.4184964 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [29] 0.0000000 0.0000000
